sentences.text: Paul Mackenzie operated his church for 16 years, attracting thousands of followers The leader of a Kenyan doomsday cult, Paul Mackenzie, has been found guilty of murdering 191 people, all but one of them children.

sentences.text: His doctrine said that education was forbidden and modern medicine was "evil".

sentences.text: A male police officer remains in hospital after being shot in the foot Four people have been arrested - including a woman on suspicion of causing grievous bodily harm and possessing a firearm - after a police officer was shot in Nottingham city centre.
sentences.article_title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: Nottinghamshire Police said the officer had approached two suspects at a bus stop in Angel Row shortly before 04:50 BST on Sunday.
sentences.article_title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: The male officer remains in hospital and is in a stable condition, the force added.
sentences.article_title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: Two women, 27 and 25, and a 24-year-old man were arrested after police stopped a vehicle in the Radford area of Nottingham on Sunday evening, while a 30-year-old man was arrested in Bedfordshire in the early hours of Monday.
sentences.article_title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: The 27-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of causing grievous bodily harm with intent, and possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life.
sentences.article_title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: The 24-year-old man and 25-year-old woman were also arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.
sentences.article_title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: Separately, after stopping a vehicle in Bedfordshire, the 30-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.
sentences.article_title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: Detectives said a gun was found at the scene Det Ch Supt Richard Bull, who is leading the investigation, described it as a "horrific crime" and said they expected to make further arrests.
sentences.article_title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: He told the BBC: "We're treating this extremely seriously.
sentences.article_title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: We've already made some arrests.
sentences.article_title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: We anticipate further arrests in the coming days, and we will not tolerate this sort of crime on our streets." Bull said he also wanted to acknowledge the actions of the "brave officer" who "went there in their job of protecting the public and as a result sustained this horrific injury".
sentences.article_title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: He added he understood that people would be concerned, but incidents like this were "extremely rare".
sentences.article_title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: "I am pleased that four arrests have now been made and hope this provides some reassurance to the public as those detained are questioned in connection with the discharge of the firearm." A large police cordon - which was put in place in Angel Row following the shooting - has now been lifted.
sentences.article_title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: ACC Rukas thanked local businesses, residents and members of the public for their patience, support and understanding while the force carried out its investigation.
sentences.article_title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: "The injured officer continues to recover in hospital and is receiving support from colleagues and loved ones," she said.
sentences.article_title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: "We ask that his privacy is respected at this time.
sentences.article_title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: The PCC added the incident highlighted the dangers of being a police officer.
sentences.article_title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: "This officer was going to speak to two individuals who were acting suspiciously, and this happened," he said.
sentences.article_title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: Labour MP for Nottingham East Nadia Whittome has told the BBC she understood the officer was "now out of surgery".
sentences.article_title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: She added: "This incident will no doubt will be damaging to the reputation of the city, especially because of our past, but I think that we also saw was an extremely rare incident that was the worst of our city.
sentences.article_title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting

sentences.text: "But we also saw the best of our city.

sentences.text: The Fantasy Bra has historically been worn by supermodels Reality TV star Kylie Jenner has sparked mixed reaction after making her Victoria's Secret Fashion Show debut in a $50m (£37m) bra.
sentences.article_title: Kylie Jenner's debut at Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in $50m bra sparks mixed reaction

sentences.text: The make-up mogul surprised the crowd at the lingerie giant's annual show on Sunday while wearing the famed Fantasy Bra, which was made of 18-carat gold and 4,410 diamonds, according to the designer.
sentences.article_title: Kylie Jenner's debut at Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in $50m bra sparks mixed reaction

sentences.text: The Fantasy Bra has been a key feature of the show over the years and wearing it is typically seen as an honour and defining moment for the chosen model.
sentences.article_title: Kylie Jenner's debut at Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in $50m bra sparks mixed reaction

sentences.text: The Kardashians star, 29, being selected to wear the piece delighted some fans, while many others criticised the brand for not giving the opportunity to a veteran supermodel.
sentences.article_title: Kylie Jenner's debut at Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in $50m bra sparks mixed reaction

sentences.text: Social media and marketing expert Joel Marlinarson says the moment was well-engineered and generated "a lot of conversation" on what it means for the "future of modelling and social media".
sentences.article_title: Kylie Jenner's debut at Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in $50m bra sparks mixed reaction

sentences.text: "Of course Kylie represents a new era of celebrity where brands are prioritising who's going to bring the most eyeballs, as opposed to who fits the cookie cutter definition of a model," he tells BBC Newsbeat.
sentences.article_title: Kylie Jenner's debut at Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in $50m bra sparks mixed reaction

sentences.text: Marlinarson says young viewers have a connection with Jenner having grown up watching her on social media and through her reality show with her Kardashian sisters.
sentences.article_title: Kylie Jenner's debut at Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in $50m bra sparks mixed reaction

sentences.text: However, he says there will be a section of the audience who remembers "the iconic Naomi Campbell era of fashion" who might see Jenner being given this moment as a "betrayal of what they know".
sentences.article_title: Kylie Jenner's debut at Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in $50m bra sparks mixed reaction

sentences.text: "Ultimately, this represents this new era of marketing where brands, particularly Victoria's Secret and legacy brands, they don't want to take risks," he says.
sentences.article_title: Kylie Jenner's debut at Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in $50m bra sparks mixed reaction

sentences.text: One said the show has "gone from iconic glamour to an influencer circus" and they felt "social media clout and performative inclusivity have replaced real modeling talent, elegance, and runway presence".
sentences.article_title: Kylie Jenner's debut at Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in $50m bra sparks mixed reaction

sentences.text: Chief creative officer at Victoria's Secret, Adam Selman, told Vogue , external that Jenner was picked for being a "cultural powerhouse".
sentences.article_title: Kylie Jenner's debut at Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in $50m bra sparks mixed reaction

sentences.text: "Kylie really extends beyond fashion, beyond culture, beyond TV, beyond one singular thing," he adds.
sentences.article_title: Kylie Jenner's debut at Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in $50m bra sparks mixed reaction

sentences.text: "That's the exact same thing that we do.
sentences.article_title: Kylie Jenner's debut at Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in $50m bra sparks mixed reaction

sentences.text: "She's an influencer with a lot of power and we are in the social media age," says the 25-year-old, who has walked the runway at New York Fashion Week.
sentences.article_title: Kylie Jenner's debut at Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in $50m bra sparks mixed reaction

sentences.text: The lingerie brand's catwalk show was scrapped after its 2018 edition drew low ratings, as well as criticism that it was sexist, outdated and lacked diversity.
sentences.article_title: Kylie Jenner's debut at Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in $50m bra sparks mixed reaction

sentences.text: It returned in 2024, with a promise to "celebrate all women" and featured more a diverse range of talent, including Ashley Graham's appearance as a plus-sized model.
sentences.article_title: Kylie Jenner's debut at Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in $50m bra sparks mixed reaction

sentences.text: Victoria's Secret created this year's Fantasy Bra in collaboration with jewellery brand Jacob & Co, who said it was the "most valuable" one ever created and took 15 artists more than 1,000 hours to create.
sentences.article_title: Kylie Jenner's debut at Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in $50m bra sparks mixed reaction

sentences.text: Nesbeth believes the focus on the bra shows "how detached we are".
sentences.article_title: Kylie Jenner's debut at Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in $50m bra sparks mixed reaction

sentences.text: "People can't eat, people can't afford to keep their lights on," she says.
sentences.article_title: Kylie Jenner's debut at Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in $50m bra sparks mixed reaction

sentences.text: "I think there's a lot of things to say about where we're focussing our attention and where we're putting our money." BBC Newsbeat has contacted Victoria's Secret.
sentences.article_title: Kylie Jenner's debut at Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in $50m bra sparks mixed reaction

sentences.text: A member of the US Air Force died after he fell while abseiling from the ceiling of a Texas stadium ahead of a college football game.
sentences.article_title: US airman dies as daredevil descent goes wrong before Texas college football game

sentences.text: Footage shows the serviceman plummet feet first to the turf midfield at San Antonio's 170ft (52 metre) high Alamodome on Saturday during a ceremony ahead of the game between the University of Texas at San Antonio and the Naval Academy.
sentences.article_title: US airman dies as daredevil descent goes wrong before Texas college football game

sentences.text: The airman, identified , external by the military as Sgt Ian Patterson, a Tactical Air Control Party instructor at Joint Base San Antonio, died in hospital.
sentences.article_title: US airman dies as daredevil descent goes wrong before Texas college football game

sentences.text: The incident is being investigated.
sentences.article_title: US airman dies as daredevil descent goes wrong before Texas college football game

sentences.text: The game between the UTSA Roadrunners and the Navy Midshipmen continued as planned following the tragic incident.
sentences.article_title: US airman dies as daredevil descent goes wrong before Texas college football game

sentences.text: A collegiate athletic association said the decision to press ahead with the fixture was made before the airman's death had been confirmed.
sentences.article_title: US airman dies as daredevil descent goes wrong before Texas college football game

sentences.text: "We extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, teammates and members of the 57th Wing," the American Conference , external said in a statement.
sentences.article_title: US airman dies as daredevil descent goes wrong before Texas college football game

sentences.text: US Air Force Brig Gen Scott Mills said in a statement issued by Nellis Air Force Base: "This tragedy is felt deeply across the 57th Wing.
sentences.article_title: US airman dies as daredevil descent goes wrong before Texas college football game

sentences.text: "Tech Sgt Patterson and his service mattered immensely to our wing." Patterson, from Fort Stewart, Georgia, had served in the US military for 15 years, according to Nellis Air Force Base.
sentences.article_title: US airman dies as daredevil descent goes wrong before Texas college football game

sentences.text: He held multiple military decorations and was in 2022 named the Air Force Special Warfare Enlisted Instructor of the Year at the Headquarters Air Force level.
sentences.article_title: US airman dies as daredevil descent goes wrong before Texas college football game

sentences.text: UTSA president Taylor Eighmy said: "I want to extend my deepest and most heartfelt sympathies to the service member's family, his fellow airmen, squadron and all those whose lives have been touched by this heartbreaking tragedy."

sentences.text: Burnham laid a wreath at the memorial garden on Monday, alongside survivor Jeff Edwards, who was one of the last children to be brought out alive from the rubble, and Welsh Secretary Stephen Kinnock.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: "It's been 60 years since one of the most horrifying tragedies this country has ever seen.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: All of those children lost," Burnham said.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: On 21 October 1966, 116 children and 28 adults were killed when a colliery spoil tip collapsed, catastrophically engulfing a primary school and surrounding houses.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: A scene of devastation caused by the mining waste tip sliding down the mountainside A survivor who spoke to the prime minister said that although she felt some "guilt" and missed those who died, it was important for her to talk about what happened.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: The prime minister said the tragedy was something his parents had told him about when he was growing up, adding that he was there to "recognise the community" and what they had been through.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: "The strength of the community today is something to see and something to feel," he said.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: "To say also to them, I don't think Aberfan was treated properly by the authorities and that also needs to be recognised.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: Burnham also addressed coal tip safety in former mining communities in south Wales.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: "It's of critical importance that we make sure that all of the remaining tips around Wales are safe indeed across the country," he said, adding he represented a former mining community in Makerfield near Manchester .
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: He said his government was providing around £140m to the Welsh government , who were "adding some extra funding themselves".
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: "There's an organisation that is being set up to manage all of these ongoing risks," he said.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: Irene Hollet, who survived the disaster, said it was important to talk about what happaned Burnham met with survivors of the tragedy, including Irene Hollett, a former pupil at Pantglas school, who said it was a difficult time but that it was important for her to speak about what happened.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: "A lot of stuff comes back to you.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: You feel grateful that you are still around 60 years on, but then you miss your friends and family that we lost at the time," she said.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: "You can fell a bit of guilt that you are still here.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: "It's a difficult time, but it's got to happen.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: All of this has to happen for nothing ever to be forgotten".
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: She said the conversation she and her fellow survivors had with the prime minister was "pleasant".
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: "We were laughing about being naughty in school, how we played truant, and we just chatted about who we were and how we are all together today," she said.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: Marilyn Brown lost her daughter Janette in the Aberfan disaster Marilyn Brown's children were in Pantglas school and she lost her daughter Janette, but her son was saved by a teacher.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: She said: "I didn't realise he was saved because he'd run up from the school and I had run up to the school, and we sort of passed one another.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: "But I didn't think Janette would die.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: In my mind, she was still alive.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: "We stood up at the top by the school, and all the women were together, and I ran from the house." Speaking to BBC, she recalled that her daughter didn't want to go to school that day, but Brown and her husband told her "you've got to".
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: She then watched her children walk up the street to school.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: "I thought, 'oh, I'll sit down now and have a cup of tea,'" she said.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: It wasn't there hardly any time at all, and my nephew run down the street and said, 'you'd better come up to the school... there's something gone wrong.'" Brown ran up the street in her slippers and remembers being stood waiting for "a long, long time" to find out what was happening.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: "We didn't realise then the children had died," she said.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: It'll never go away, and I hope people will remember, and they have today." Burnham has been described by survivors of Aberfan as 'very down-to-earth' and 'respectful' Brown described Burnham as "very nice, very down-to-earth and very, very respectful".
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: While sat around a table with him, Brown said she "didn't say about losing a child" or that she "was a survivor".
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: Burnham met pupils including Ellis, 10, whose granddad travelled across the valley to Aberfan to help with the rescue effort.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: "It means a lot to me and he tells me stories," said Ellis, who described visiting the memorial garden as "emotional".
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: Holly, aged 10 from Caegarw, also told the prime minister she had a personal connection with the tragedy.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: "I told him about my godmother's daughter being one of the children who passed away in the disaster," she said.
sentences.article_title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'

sentences.text: It means a lot for us to be here." When a colliery waste tip collapsed, slurry crashed into Pantglas Junior School, killing 116 children and 28 adults Burnham stopped to chat with local residents after visiting the garden before heading to the nearby community centre.

sentences.text: A three-hour documentary on the tech fraudster Elizabeth Holmes has raked in a whopping $15 million (£11.25m) on its box office debut, despite a limited run at 855 screens across the US and Canada.
sentences.article_title: Elizabeth Holmes  documentary stuns with huge box office debut

sentences.text: The eagerly anticipated film, You Can See Everything, finds Holmes at home in California in 2023, during the month before she began an 11-year prison sentence.
sentences.article_title: Elizabeth Holmes  documentary stuns with huge box office debut

sentences.text: It was co-directed by comedian Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim who find themselves embroiled in the story, growing suspicious that Holmes and her partner are withholding information.
sentences.article_title: Elizabeth Holmes  documentary stuns with huge box office debut

sentences.text: US publication Deadline noted the film had enjoyed "easily the second best opening ever for a [non-music] documentary at the box office", after Michael Moore's 2004 film about the invasion of Iraq, Fahrenheit 9/11.
sentences.article_title: Elizabeth Holmes  documentary stuns with huge box office debut

sentences.text: Ticket sales at the box office were enough for second place behind Paramount's new video game adaptation, Street Fighter, which opened to $31 million in North America and $51.1 million globally.
sentences.article_title: Elizabeth Holmes  documentary stuns with huge box office debut

sentences.text: You Can See Everything also secured the largest debut for any film playing on under 1,000 screens since 2006's Borat, which scored $26 million.
sentences.article_title: Elizabeth Holmes  documentary stuns with huge box office debut

sentences.text: Holmes was convicted of defrauding investors in her medical testing company Theranos, fuelling a media circus that has been chronicled in books, podcasts and the mini-series The Dropout, starring Amanda Seyfried.
sentences.article_title: Elizabeth Holmes  documentary stuns with huge box office debut

sentences.text: In You Can See Everything, Canadian comedian Fielder - known for his awkward, deadpan and at-times surreal humour, on shows including The Rehearsal and The Curse - places himself inside the action, once again blurring the lines between documentary, social experiment and prank show.
sentences.article_title: Elizabeth Holmes  documentary stuns with huge box office debut

sentences.text: We see notorious Silicon Valley founder Holmes and her partner Billy Evans invite a sceptical film crew to document her every move, 34 days before she's sent to prison.
sentences.article_title: Elizabeth Holmes  documentary stuns with huge box office debut

sentences.text: Seyfried appears in the hybrid documentary to re-enact events and scenes that the documentary crew could not film or needed to reconstruct.
sentences.article_title: Elizabeth Holmes  documentary stuns with huge box office debut

sentences.text: The first teaser trailer dropped last month, right after the film's surprise premiere at the Telluride Film Festival in Colorado.
sentences.article_title: Elizabeth Holmes  documentary stuns with huge box office debut

sentences.text: It went viral and launched many online memes of Holmes unblinkingly asking first-time filmmaker, Fielder: "Why would I deceive you?" The stranger-than-fiction documentary has garnered rave reviews and is already being talked about as an Oscar contender as we head into awards season.
sentences.article_title: Elizabeth Holmes  documentary stuns with huge box office debut

sentences.text: Remarkable really for a documentary that was produced in secret over three years, and which no-one really knew about until recently.
sentences.article_title: Elizabeth Holmes  documentary stuns with huge box office debut

sentences.text: The Guardian awarded the film five stars , external , calling it "a modern masterpiece of deceit", stressing how "TV's grand illusionist meets his match when he moves in with Theranos founder and her family".
sentences.article_title: Elizabeth Holmes  documentary stuns with huge box office debut

sentences.text: The Financial Times , external also offered five stars describing the documentary as "a mind-bending revelation".
sentences.article_title: Elizabeth Holmes  documentary stuns with huge box office debut

sentences.text: The New York Times , external said viewers see Holmes and Fielder "joust in a dizzying movie about truth, reality and the contours of knowledge".
sentences.article_title: Elizabeth Holmes  documentary stuns with huge box office debut

sentences.text: The buzz around the film is likely to see it be in the running, at least, for a nomination for best documentary feature at next year's Academy Awards, though no documentary has ever been nominated for the main prize of best picture.
sentences.article_title: Elizabeth Holmes  documentary stuns with huge box office debut

sentences.text: This video can not be played WATCH: The father and son on opposite sides of Alberta’s separation referendum People in the province of Alberta head to the polls on Monday to decide whether to hold a binding referendum at a later date on separating from Canada.
sentences.article_title: Alberta heads to polls to decide whether to hold vote on separation from Canada

sentences.text: The vote was called earlier this year by the leader of the province, Danielle Smith, after a grassroots group gathered about 300,000 signatures on a petition that asked for a binding referendum on separation.
sentences.article_title: Alberta heads to polls to decide whether to hold vote on separation from Canada

sentences.text: Many of those who support separation say the oil-rich province's economic growth has been stifled by the environmental policies of Canada's central government in Ottawa.
sentences.article_title: Alberta heads to polls to decide whether to hold vote on separation from Canada

sentences.text: But those who want Alberta to remain part of Canada - who include Prime Minister Mark Carney - have called for the country to show unity in the face of external pressures.
sentences.article_title: Alberta heads to polls to decide whether to hold vote on separation from Canada

sentences.text: Polls have suggested that the majority of Albertans would vote to remain in Canada, though the pre-vote debate alone has proven divisive.
sentences.article_title: Alberta heads to polls to decide whether to hold vote on separation from Canada

sentences.text: Another group collected signatures for its own petition that opposed separation, which was signed by more than 400,000 people.
sentences.article_title: Alberta heads to polls to decide whether to hold vote on separation from Canada

sentences.text: The province's population is about five million people.
sentences.article_title: Alberta heads to polls to decide whether to hold vote on separation from Canada

sentences.text: If Albertans do vote on Monday to move ahead with a binding referendum, that could happen as soon as 2027, Smith has said.
sentences.article_title: Alberta heads to polls to decide whether to hold vote on separation from Canada

sentences.text: Nottingham Forest's Morgan Gibbs-White failed to respond to two police letters, according to court documents England and Nottingham Forest attacking midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White has been handed a £1,000 court bill after his Range Rover was caught running a red light.
sentences.article_title: Morgan Gibbs-White fined after his car ran red light

sentences.text: The 26-year-old's vehicle was caught on camera going past a set of lights in West Bridgford, Nottinghamshire, 1.1 seconds after they turned red.
sentences.article_title: Morgan Gibbs-White fined after his car ran red light

sentences.text: Gibbs-White, who earned his first England cap in 2024, failed to respond to two police letters asking him to confirm if he had been driving at the time of the red light offence, according to court documents.
sentences.article_title: Morgan Gibbs-White fined after his car ran red light

sentences.text: Last Tuesday, he was convicted by a court of failing to provide the identity of a driver at the time of an offence.
sentences.article_title: Morgan Gibbs-White fined after his car ran red light

sentences.text: Nottinghamshire Police put out an alert on Gibbs-White's car when the force tried to investigate the traffic light incident, and found the number plate registered with the DVLA was one letter different from what was on the vehicle.
sentences.article_title: Morgan Gibbs-White fined after his car ran red light

sentences.text: Staffordshire Police then pulled over the Range Rover in April and confirmed it belonged to Gibbs-White.
sentences.article_title: Morgan Gibbs-White fined after his car ran red light

sentences.text: At Southern Derbyshire Magistrates' Court, he was fined £660, given six penalty points on his licence and ordered to pay £120 in costs and a £264 victim surcharge.
sentences.article_title: Morgan Gibbs-White fined after his car ran red light

sentences.text: Gibbs-White was called up to Thomas Tuchel's recent England squad for the Nations League A court official said Gibbs-White did not enter a plea or mitigation, and was sentenced behind closed doors under the fast-track Single Justice Procedure.
sentences.article_title: Morgan Gibbs-White fined after his car ran red light

sentences.text: Court papers show a Nottinghamshire Police camera caught Gibbs-White's car going past a red traffic light at 15:17 GMT on 28 January in Radcliffe Road.
sentences.article_title: Morgan Gibbs-White fined after his car ran red light

sentences.text: "At the time of the offence, the vehicle was captured failing to comply with a red light signal, the time into the red light was recorded as 1.1 seconds," a police worker wrote in her statement.
sentences.article_title: Morgan Gibbs-White fined after his car ran red light

sentences.text: Gibbs-White was banned from driving for six months in May last year after he was caught speeding six times in the space of three months.
sentences.article_title: Morgan Gibbs-White fined after his car ran red light

sentences.text: Assistant Chief Constable Ryan Henderson said police consider the risk to the public as "low" An email threatening that "an explosive device" is located within hundreds of schools in Northern Ireland is being treated as a "hoax" by the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI).
sentences.article_title: Schools 'explosive device' email a hoax, say police

sentences.text: Assistant Chief Constable Ryan Henderson said police take "incidents of this nature very seriously" however "at this stage we consider risk to the public as low".
sentences.article_title: Schools 'explosive device' email a hoax, say police

sentences.text: Some schools have closed after receiving the email, however others have decided to stay open and are taking advice from the PSNI.
sentences.article_title: Schools 'explosive device' email a hoax, say police

sentences.text: Police Scotland said they are investigating emails sent to schools and are also treating threats as a hoax.
sentences.article_title: Schools 'explosive device' email a hoax, say police

sentences.text: One school in Lambeg emailed parents to say that they should "come immediately" and collect children adding: "Please don't panic the children are all safe." The email originated from outside the UK police say and similar emails have been received by some schools across the UK.
sentences.article_title: Schools 'explosive device' email a hoax, say police

sentences.text: The PSNI said up to 300 schools have reported receiving the same emailed message which contained a generalised threat.
sentences.article_title: Schools 'explosive device' email a hoax, say police

sentences.text: "Checks have not, at this time, resulted in anything untoward," added the PSNI.
sentences.article_title: Schools 'explosive device' email a hoax, say police

sentences.text: "Based on enquiries and information to date, police are treating this email, which originated from outside the UK, as a hoax." Henderson said police "understand the concern in the community, not to mention the disruption it has caused in some school communities and for students and parents".
sentences.article_title: Schools 'explosive device' email a hoax, say police

sentences.text: "We will continue to liaise with schools impacted and have been working closely with the Department of Education and the Education Authority this morning to provide reassurance." Police enquires into the email are continuing.
sentences.article_title: Schools 'explosive device' email a hoax, say police

sentences.text: In a statement he added: "Schools should continue to operate as normal." "I recognise that this has caused huge alarm and distress among pupils, parents and school staff and I understand that schools have had to make decisions in the best interests of their pupils and staff.
sentences.article_title: Schools 'explosive device' email a hoax, say police

sentences.text: This has unfortunately led to a number of school closures.
sentences.article_title: Schools 'explosive device' email a hoax, say police

sentences.text: Parents were given the option to collect their children from the school.

sentences.text: Nora Xhemha also collected her children.

sentences.article_title: Schools 'explosive device' email a hoax, say police

sentences.text: "We don't know what is going on.
sentences.article_title: Schools 'explosive device' email a hoax, say police

sentences.text: "There's been nothing from the Education Authority, there's been nothing from CCMS [Council for Catholic Maintained Schools], bar two letters that are more or less telling us absolutely nothing," she said.
sentences.article_title: Schools 'explosive device' email a hoax, say police

sentences.text: Robinson said she feels that principals have been left to make the decisions themselves.
sentences.article_title: Schools 'explosive device' email a hoax, say police

sentences.text: "We need guidance in the event these things happen.
sentences.article_title: Schools 'explosive device' email a hoax, say police

sentences.text: "It's wholly unacceptable when we're dealing with children".
sentences.article_title: Schools 'explosive device' email a hoax, say police

sentences.article_title: Schools 'explosive device' email a hoax, say police

sentences.article_title: Schools 'explosive device' email a hoax, say police

sentences.article_title: Schools 'explosive device' email a hoax, say police

sentences.text: "While some disruption was caused, the majority of schools remained open.

sentences.text: "We thank school leaders and staff for their professional response to a difficult and challenging situation." In a statement the Council for Catholic Maintained Schools (CCMS) said they recognise the message will have caused "concern and anxiety among pupils, parents and staff".

sentences.text: Bereaved families affected by severe delays paying out civil service pensions could face an "unjust" tax bill, the government has been warned.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Under HMRC rules, certain lump sum pension payments must be paid within two years of the pension scheme being notified of a death to remain tax-free.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Conservative MP Sir Geoffrey Clifton-Brown, who chairs Parliament's Public Accounts Committee, said it was "unconscionable" some families could face a "death tax" through no fault of their own.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: The Cabinet Office said that if delays caused a tax charge there were existing avenues to claim compensation, such as the Pensions Ombudsman.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: However, the ombudsman is currently advising that standard complaints are only likely to be resolved within 18 months, with more complex cases facing a longer wait.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: The Civil Service Pension scheme manages the pensions of 1.7 million public sector workers in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Outsourcing firm Capita took over the administration of the scheme from a company called MyCSP in December 2025, saying it inherited a backlog of more than 86,000 cases.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Despite a two-year transition period to prepare for the takeover, problems have persisted and by February the backlog had grown to 120,000 cases.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Retired civil servants and bereaved families have been left waiting months for pension payments, with some struggling to pay bills.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Civil service pension backlog 'overwhelmed' Capita, boss says Emergency loans offered to civil servants waiting on pensions Retired civil servants left in pension limbo According to the latest figures up to 30 September , external , 1,643 outstanding cases of bereavement or death in service are more than 100 days old.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Of these, only 301 are in scope to be paid within 15 days.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: The PCS union, which represents civil servants, said that while not all these cases would ultimately be affected by the two-year tax rule, there were "serious questions" over how long they would remain unresolved.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: If someone dies before the age of 75, a pension lump sum death benefit is only tax-free if it is paid within two years of the pension scheme first becoming aware of the death, and if the value is below the deceased's Lump Sum and Death Benefit Allowance.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: The payment would be taxed at the same rate as the beneficiary's income tax rate.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Sir Geoffrey has written to Cabinet Office Minister Louise Haigh to urge the government to confirm the bereaved families affected will not face this "unjust financial penalty".
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: His letter came after BBC Radio 4's Money Box Live highlighted the potential tax liability.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Sir Geoffrey said "the chaos currently engulfing the Civil Service Pension Scheme means that the likelihood of death benefit payments being made within two years is slim".
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: He warned "a significant number" of family members "will be watching the clock quickly tick down to a year, as the maladministration of the scheme enters its tenth month".
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: He added: "This is an additional stress they should not have to bear." Money Box Live: Capita, What Went Wrong?
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Money Box Live looks at what is going on with Capita, which administers millions of people's pensions Rob Wassell, 58, has been waiting almost two years for the lump sum from his brother's civil service pension, following his death.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: On 22 October it will be two years since the pension scheme was notified of his death so if he does not receive the payment in just a few days times, it could face being taxed.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Rob, who contacted the BBC's Money Box programme about his case, said he had been phoning Capita with increasing "desperation" as his situation dragged on.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: "It's a bitter pill to swallow to have to pay tax for something which was not my fault," he said.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: "It creates unnecessary worry and anguish through the process, which is already in itself difficult." Rob said he needed the money to cover the estate costs he had to pay for his brother and fill a £20,000 hole in his savings.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: However, he said it was "heartbreaking" to hear of other cases where people needed the money just to survive.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Rob added that the idea that he might face "another battle" to recoup the tax through compensation made it feel like "you just want to give up".
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Rob is hoping the government will waive the tax due for people in his situation Fran Heathcote, head of the PCS union, said it would be "a profound injustice" if families faced a further financial penalty because of Capita's failures.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: "If that does happen, the government should be ashamed that families are being made to pay the price for failures that are entirely outside their control," she said.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: A spokesperson for the Cabinet Office, which has overall responsibility for the Civil Service Pension Scheme, said: "The service levels following the move to Capita have been completely unacceptable and we are committed to ensuring no member is left financially worse off.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: "We are continuing to hold Capita to account, including holding back nearly £10m in payments, and are doing everything in our power to ensure that individuals do not experience delays.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: "If delays cause a tax charge, existing avenues for complaints can provide financial redress or compensation to cover losses." A Capita spokesperson said: "We are deeply sorry for the frustration that the administration of the Civil Service Pension Scheme has caused members and their families.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Pickstock Telford said the site would employ about 90 staff once it was fully operational Residents of a small south Scotland village say they fear losing their "quiet life" after work started on a £24m meat processing plant nearby.

sentences.text: Passengers who play loud music on buses in England could be fined up to £100 under an attempt by the government to crack down on antisocial behaviour.
sentences.article_title: People playing loud music on buses could face £100 fine

sentences.text: The measures also seek to tackle littering, vaping and threatening behaviour to help improve journeys on all forms of public transport.
sentences.article_title: People playing loud music on buses could face £100 fine

sentences.text: Offenders on buses could be issued with the fines under new powers for local authorities.
sentences.article_title: People playing loud music on buses could face £100 fine

sentences.text: There have been laws against playing loud music, as well as singing, on trains since 2005 but the government will remind rail passengers of this with the launch of a national campaign asking people to "share the carriage, not the noise".
sentences.article_title: People playing loud music on buses could face £100 fine

sentences.text: The proposed crackdown has been welcomed by campaigners, but some have questioned how it can be enforced.
sentences.article_title: People playing loud music on buses could face £100 fine

sentences.text: "We've all been on the train when someone starts blasting music or videos from their phone.
sentences.article_title: People playing loud music on buses could face £100 fine

sentences.text: It gets on your nerves and can quickly spoil the journey," said Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
sentences.article_title: People playing loud music on buses could face £100 fine

sentences.text: The phenomenon has been given many terms - including loudcasting or sodcasting - and in recent years, Ofcom, YouGov and Transport for London (TfL) have all published polls showing the vast majority of people dislike it.
sentences.article_title: People playing loud music on buses could face £100 fine

sentences.text: The rail campaign will be launched across operator websites, social media, and in carriages.
sentences.article_title: People playing loud music on buses could face £100 fine

sentences.text: Under existing powers, those who are asked to stop and refuse could be removed from a train or fined up to £1,000.
sentences.article_title: People playing loud music on buses could face £100 fine

sentences.text: The government also said it had issued new guidance to local authorities on powers - which were introduced earlier this year - to help them crackdown on loud music and other antisocial behaviour on buses in England.
sentences.article_title: People playing loud music on buses could face £100 fine

sentences.text: These new powers allow them to impose new rules on buses, but still need to be signed off by the Transport Secretary Those who commit offences could face fixed penalties of up to £100.
sentences.article_title: People playing loud music on buses could face £100 fine

sentences.text: The government says bus drivers will not be responsible for enforcing the new rules.
sentences.article_title: People playing loud music on buses could face £100 fine

sentences.text: It says authorised officers, including Transport Safety Officers and the Police, will  deal with the incidents.
sentences.article_title: People playing loud music on buses could face £100 fine

sentences.text: Commenting on how fines will be enforced, Chris McDonald, Minister for Science, Research and Innovation, told BBC Breakfast that passengers can complain to staff  "or the British Transport Police if they wish".

sentences.text: The spokesperson added that the BBC "takes independence and transparency incredibly seriously, and we must ensure we are meeting the highest standards".

sentences.text: They said although statisticians' work had sometimes been recognised with their names on the BBC website, "they never made editorial decisions".

sentences.text: According to The Telegraph , external , a job advert for the 2027 secondment said a successful candidate would have "the ability to influence decision making, working with credibility and proactively with customers to share knowledge and information".

sentences.text: A now-removed blog post written by one civil servant about their placements showed a secondee describing how they had drafted copy for the news website.

sentences.text: Under the scheme, it is understood that statisticians explain data in writing that can be incorporated into stories, but they do not write the copy itself.
sentences.article_title: BBC pauses civil service secondment scheme

sentences.text: Secondees' contributions can be incorporated into journalism that scrutinises the current government, as well as all political parties.
sentences.article_title: BBC pauses civil service secondment scheme

sentences.text: The seconded statisticians also have to adhere to the Civil Service Code of Practice for Statistics.
sentences.article_title: BBC pauses civil service secondment scheme

sentences.text: Chancellor John Healey is planning to increase taxes on the bank sector, senior banking executives have told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Healey has described banks as part of "the crown jewels" of the UK economy, but leaders in the sector have said it will be "on the menu" at the Budget in two weeks' time.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: The biggest four banks collectively made about £15bn profit in the first six months of this year, and trade unions have called for them to face additional taxes.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: The trade body for the banking sector, UK Finance, warned "further increases in bank taxes would weaken competitiveness, discourage investment and job creation, and work against the government's ambition to deliver growth in every postcode".

sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: What is the Budget and what could be in it?
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: There are a number of ways the chancellor could extract more money from the sector.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: One option is for Healey is to reverse a reduction in the surcharge that banks pay on corporation tax, from 8% to 3%, introduced in 2023, by Conservative chancellor Jeremy Hunt.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Critics argue this would be unfair noting the cut coincided with a rise in corporation tax from 19% to 25%.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Healey could also raise the bank levy - a small percentage charged on loans.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: The BBC understands that the Treasury is leaning towards changing the surcharge if they were to go ahead as it is easier to change an existing tax rather than impose a new windfall tax.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: Reversing the 2023 surcharge rate would raise around £2bn.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: However, the last government was persuaded that adding 8% on top of corporation tax of 25% would leave UK banks struggling to compete with European and US rivals - so it may be that it is raised, but not all the way back to the 8% level.

sentences.text: Speaking to the press in Bangkok, Healey praised the role banks play in the British economy.
sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.article_title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget

sentences.text: The operators of Newby Island landfill have been ordered to take action over odours Milpitas, an affluent city in California's Silicon Valley tech hub, has an odour problem.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: For decades, residents have had to endure rank smells wafting from industrial sites, among them a 342-acre landfill.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "When I first moved here, I could not open my window for over 10 years," says Chia-Ling Kong, an engineer for a tech firm who lives around half a mile from the dump.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: While things have got better in recent years, Kong says she and her neighbours must still contend with around "two or three hours of bad smells a day".
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Perhaps befitting Silicon Valley, the community is putting its hopes in technology.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: The operators of Newby Island landfill have been ordered by local authorities to use drones and install monitors to systematically track and measure the chemicals responsible for bad odours.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: They have also been told to automate the collection of landfill gases responsible for smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Kong is optimistic a data-driven approach will make a difference.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Hopefully with this continuous monitoring, it makes it easier to pinpoint problems at the moment it starts." The operators of the landfill say they are committed to operating it safely and protecting air quality.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Just like in Milpitas, where Kong is part of a citizen's campaign against the odours, communities around the world are raising a stink about bad smells making day-to-day life miserable.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Sometimes a rubbish dump is to blame, or it might be a sewage treatment works, or a reeking factory.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: When the complaints start stacking up, resolving them is not always simple.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Many countries have no regulations in place dictating how to manage smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In the US, for example, the Environmental Protection Agency does not regulate environmental odours as a pollutant.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This leaves states and local governments to take charge of the issue.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Urban sprawl is often part of the problem, bringing communities closer to stinky facilities that may historically have been kept at a distance.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This is creating more demand for technologies to monitor and prevent smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Odour consultant Micheal Bull says people are increasingly concerned about neighbourhood stinks.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "You're getting developments being built nearer to odorous processes… as land has become more valuable, there is also infilling," Bull says.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: He is speaking about his experiences in the UK, but it's a similar story in many parts of the world.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Bad smells from waste sites are among the most difficult to resolve The technologies used to tackle industrial pongs generally fall into three categories: they absorb odours; convert them into something less smelly through a chemical reaction; or burn them away.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Experts on fixing industrial odours say that the best technologies, when used correctly, can remove 90% or more of the target compounds responsible for smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: But this can be expensive and some operators opt for simpler and cheaper solutions.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: These include masking odours from landfill or sewage processing by spraying giant quantities of deodorisers.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Odour experts contacted for this article were dubious about the effectiveness of such industrial scale air fresheners.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "In my view they're not likely to change the odours," says Bull, who likens them to fabric conditioner.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Bad smells from waste sites – a common cause of complaints – are among the stinkiest and most difficult to resolve, according to Carlos Diaz, an environmental consultant based in Spain.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Landfill is difficult to treat because you have a very large surface," he says.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In some places at least, technology is making a real difference.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Residents in Des Moines, Iowa, have long complained of the so-called Eastside Funk, a putrid scent that residents report drifts over parts of the city.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: A study commissioned by city authorities showed that a trio of industrial meat companies were among culprits.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Within 10 miles, there's about half a million people," says Dalton Jacobus, who works in the Department of Neighborhood Services.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "If the winds are out of the wrong direction, 100,000 people can be in the middle of that odour plume." The authorities are now paying around $240,000 (£182,000) a year on technology to track the stink, so they can take action.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "What we wanted to do was build a ring of odour monitors around the facilities that we suspected of emitting odours," says Jacobus.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: The monitors, which measure levels of chemical compounds in the air, work in combination with a weather station to provide real-time data on the concentrations that are coming from each facility based off the wind patterns.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This has put an end to finger pointing about who's to blame each time a smell sparks complaints, says Jacobus.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Smithfield Foods, which operates a meat processing in Des Moines, says it has invested $2m to install a regenerative thermal oxidiser that destroys the chemicals associated with bad smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Even so, the company says it does not believe it is the source of odour complaints.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Before installing the monitors – which some local companies help pay for – officials in Des Moines would drive out to the source of a complaint to sniff the air.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Relying on the human nose to sniff out industrial smells is still commonplace.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Claudia Barrios Obregón from Kunak, the company behind the monitors in Des Moines, says: "Right now, the way that cities control or measure odours is olfactometry: a human panel measures and gives an opinion of what the odour is like.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: But that's not that realistic." The Spanish company's monitors are an example of so-called electronic noses that make it easier to detect smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Whatever technology is used, it can be hard to keep everyone happy, as smells are so subjective.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Unfortunately, the general rule is that the nastier we perceive the odour to be, the more sensitive towards it we are," says Johan Lundström, a professor in the science of smell at the Karolinska Institute in Stockholm, Sweden.

sentences.text: Rainmaker's drones were used over Alaska this year On 23 August, Cooper Freeman had no idea clouds above his head were being filled with a silver compound in order to cause rainfall.

sentences.text: Neither did thousands of other residents in Homer, Alaska, who later discovered a  start-up called Rainmaker conducted an experiment in that region using cloud-seeding technology.

sentences.text: The company, based in El Segundo California, claims it produced 19 million US gallons of water in the sky in three hours.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: This approach to weather modification, now more than 80-years-old, involves using planes and drones to disperse compounds such as silver iodide into clouds to form ice crystals.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Those crystals eventually become large enough to fall as rain or snow, depending on the temperatures below.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Essentially, cloud seeding speeds up the natural process of water vapor condensing inside of clouds.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Gravity then pulls those crystals to the ground.
sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.article_title: Rainmakers: The drones used to seed clouds

sentences.text: Farmer Steve Cargil is now paid $200,000 a year for hosting a solar farm on his land Steve Cargil's family has farmed the flat, dry land around Uvalde, a small city in southwest Texas, since 1953.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Cargil, 67, had always assumed that one of his three children would eventually take it over, the way he had from his father.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: But that assumption took a hit one night in 2018 after a violent hailstorm.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Cargil and his son, Ryan, had spent months nursing crops of cabbage and onions to harvest.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Then a storm rolled through and destroyed them overnight.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "I remember my son saying, 'Dad, I just don't know if I can do this.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: You do everything right, and we work so hard, and you come out one morning and it's all gone'," Cargil says.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Cargil's farm was at risk of ending with him, he says, with none of his three children wanting to farm full time.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: For years, that left him wondering what would happen to the land, and to his own retirement, since farmers rarely have a pension to fall back on.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Then in 2001 Cargil signed a deal to lease 600 acres of his land, about a quarter of the total, to a company called OCI Energy which built a vast solar farm.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "Never in my wildest dreams did I think that a solar project would be on my farm," Cargil says.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Looking back now, he calls it a blessing.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: The lease, which pays Cargil $200,000 (£150,000) a year, has let him keep his farm running through a punishing drought.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: He has been able to concentrate his water irrigation allowance on the land he still farms, and he has stopped losing sleep over rises in the price of things such as diesel and fertiliser.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Solar farms can stretch out across the flat lands of Texas On hot afternoons, when demand for power peaks, solar is now regularly supplying around a third of the electricity used across Texas, says Mark Stover, executive director of the Texas Solar and Storage Association.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: He says that the solar boom is being driven by two main things.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Firstly, it is cheap and quick to connect solar farms to Texas' power grid, which is separate to the rest of the US.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Secondly, Texas has a huge and growing appetite for electricity, driven by a burgeoning population.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Between 2015 and 2025, Texas's population increased by 15.8%, , external making it one of the fastest-growing states in the nation.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "We need a whole lot of power in Texas, and we need it quickly," Stover says.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Solar has also become inexpensive.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: James Scott, vice president of project development at OCI, says the technology has had years of small manufacturing gains that brought the price down to the point where it is now the cheapest way to generate power in the state.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "No one would have believed that 20 years ago," Scott says.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Once a project is built, he says, the price of the electricity it produces can be fixed for decades, since the fuel, sunlight, is free.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "We'll charge you $40 a megawatt hour for the next 25 years," Scott says, adding that large buyers such as Amazon and Apple value being able to lock in a price for that long.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: By contrast, new coal plants in the US produce power at nearly $90 megawatts per hour, says the Energy Information Administration.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Farmers have become central to that growth because solar developers need large stretches of flat land.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Stover says the industry is now paying out multigenerational income to families through leases that typically run 25 to 30 years and rise in value each year, letting some retire, set up family trusts, or simply keep a farm solvent.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Stover argues solar's footprint is smaller than critics assume.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "The industry is utilizing less than 0.15% of Texas land," he says.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: In Franklin County, in northeast Texas, a small group of residents has spent the past few years fighting its growth.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: BF Hicks, a local lawyer whose family has owned land in the county since the 1800s, says he watched neighbours sign 30-year leases with solar companies and bulldozers clear centuries-old oak trees near his property.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: He describes a summer when smoke from burning cleared land hung over his town for weeks.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "It got real personal," he says, when a solar farm was built next to his family's cemetery.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: His relatives have been buried here dating back two centuries.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: David Truesdale, a retired federal law enforcement agent who moved to the county to get away from city life, says he became involved after learning that a neighbouring solar project would sit near his home.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: And that under Texan law no environmental review was required.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "We're destroying the world as we're trying to save it," Truesdale says of the land clearing he has seen.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: He also points to the large lithium-ion battery units installed alongside many solar farms, drawing a comparison to fires that have occasionally engulfed similar batteries in electric bikes.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "If one of those things catches fire, they go off in series, so each one will progressively cause another one to go off," he says.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Lawyer BF Hicks fights the building of new solar farms Both men say their objections are not about politics.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Franklin County is solidly conservative, but its residents helped push through one of the state's first county-level moratoriums on new solar construction, before it was later rescinded under legal pressure from developers.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Their complaints echo a broader unease that has followed solar's expansion into rural Texas - worries about visual impact, water runoff after land is cleared, and battery storage units that scorch their land.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: President Trump has called solar and wind power "farmer destroying" and moved to unwind tax credits for renewable projects.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "There is an acceptance that these technologies bring reliability benefits to the grid," he says.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: Back in Uvalde, Steve Cargil says that while he has no plans to retire any time soon, he is more positive that the farm might make it to a fifth generation after all, now that the solar farm has put a floor under its finances.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom

sentences.text: "You're better off being lucky than being smart," Cargil says, echoing something his father used to tell him.
sentences.article_title: How the oil capital of the US welcomed a solar power boom
