sentences.text: Farmer Juan Ángel Izquierdo says it is hard not to worry about wildfires In a small green meadow in the Gredos mountains, west of Madrid, a couple of dozen cows belonging to Juan Ángel Izquierdo and his family are grazing.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The only noise is the gentle clang of the bells around the animals' necks.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: This would be an idyllic scene were it not for the blackened pine and oak trees all around, the legacy of a devastating recent wildfire.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It was immense, I've never seen anything like it," says Izquierdo, whose family have been farming here for 200 years.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The fire, in late July, merged with two others, burning a total of around 80,000 hectares (200,000 acres), making it the biggest blaze Spain has ever registered.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: It consumed more than two-thirds of Izquierdo's land and killed 12 of his 85 cows.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Another eight animals had to be put down because of their injuries.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: All the hay he had gathered to feed his cows in the winter was also burned.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "For us farmers, the summers are becoming more and more worrying, because they are getting hotter," he says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It rains less, the wet season ends earlier and the autumn starts much later." For farmers, such conditions are synonymous with fires.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "If you don't think about the wildfires too much, you feel okay," Izquierdo says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "But when a fire starts in a nearby village you start wondering – 'and what if we're next?'." Wildfires are one of several symptoms of climate change which in recent years have had a substantial impact on Spain's economy, as well as contributing to shocking human tragedies.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: World Weather Attribution, an international research organisation, found that the extreme conditions that drove record-breaking fires in Spain and Portugal in 2025 were 40 times more likely , external to happen due to the warming climate.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The ultimate reason for the greater frequency and intensity of these kinds of fires has to be attributed to the increase in greenhouse gases caused mainly by the generalised use of fossil fuels," said Ernesto Rodríguez Camino, president of the Spanish Meteorology Association.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The Socialist Prime Minister, Pedro Sánchez, has described the fires in dramatic terms, placing Spain in the front line of an environmental crisis.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The climate emergency kills," he said in July, during a visit to the southern province of Almería where a wildfire claimed 15 lives.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Research found that extreme heat and resulting fires in Spain were now 40 times more likely This year, around 300,000 hectares of land have been burned in Spain, according to the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS), approximately half the total affected in the entire European Union.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The local authorities in Castilla y León, the region most heavily affected by this year's massive fire near Madrid, are offering compensation – between €5,500 ($6,300; £4,700) and €25,000 ($29,000; £21,000) to each farmer – depending on the damage suffered.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: But Izquierdo estimates that this will cover less than half of his losses.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: For decades, Spain's warm climate has been a boon for one of its other biggest industries - tourism.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Sun-drenched resorts along the Mediterranean coast, and in the Balearic and Canary Islands, have driven the country's growth as a tourist hub.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: This year, close to 100 million foreigners are expected to come to Spain, making it the second most-visited country in the world, just behind France.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Yet there are signs that the heat is becoming too much for some travellers.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: However, this summer tested their tolerance of heat, with the country registering a record-breaking 61 days of heatwaves that continued into early September.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Toledo repeatedly saw temperatures in excess of 40C.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It's quite difficult to do the tours in the summer," says guide Diego Esteban, of the company VisiToledo.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "We need to adapt, whether it is those of us who work in the tourism industry or the locals." When leading tours in the summer months, Esteban makes sure that there are frequent stops, drinking water is provided and that the itineraries include plenty of shade.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: However, he would like to see more shade and drinking fountains available.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: He says the heat has started to change the timing of the tourist season, bringing many more visitors during the cooler months of spring and autumn.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Warmer summers have also encouraged the so-called "coolcation" trend, whereby Spanish travellers seek out cooler areas to spend their holidays, typically in the north of the country.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Another consequence of Spain's warming climate has been drought.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: In 2024, after three years of minimal rainfall, the north-eastern region of Catalonia temporarily introduced stringent restrictions on water use, including a 25% reduction for industry and an 80% reduction for crop farming.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Heavy rainfall since then has lifted the restrictions, but the drought had a major impact on the local economy.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The most dramatic and tragic natural phenomenon Spain has seen in recent years were flash floods that killed 237 people in the east of the country in October 2024, centred on the Valencia region.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Spanish meteorological research group Climatoc-Lab described it as "a manifestation of how global warming alters the hydrological cycle".
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The Valencia Chamber of Commerce estimated that the floods caused €4.5bn in direct damage.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Thousands of businesses were affected, some literally washed away by the floodwater, while others were able to resume operations after a lengthy recovery.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It was a disaster, both in terms of the lives lost and the impact on businesses, on workers, employers and ordinary people," says Laura Llácer Álvarez, manager of the Fepeval federation of industrial parks in the Valencia region.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Spain's geographical position, along with its climate and topography, make it unusually vulnerable as global temperatures increase.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Germanwatch, an independent environmental organisation, ranked Spain the world's 20th most affected country in its climate risk index for 2024, just behind Nigeria and Mali.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Yet there are those who see an upside for the economy.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "Climate change affects how we produce, how we invest and how we consume," says Julián Cubero, head of economics of climate change at economic think tank BBVA Research.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: He points to how heat can act as a drag on economic activity.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "We all work worse when it's hot," he says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: However, he adds, a greener economy can create new jobs with greater productivity.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The key is to realise that if we don't act, growth will slow down, and if it's handled right it can become an opportunity," he says.

sentences.text: Europe's heatwave has boosted demand for battery storage systems As heatwaves scorched Europe this summer, workers at a US battery company noticed an uptick in demand.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: San Diego-based Unigrid sells a nine kilowatt hour battery for people's homes.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sweltering European homeowners were apparently looking for ways of storing power when it was available from the grid at lower rates.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: They could then run air conditioners more cheaply, off the battery, during the worst heat of the day.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We have requests coming from Spain, France, Germany, The Netherlands," says Darren Tan, co-founder and chief executive.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We've shipped the first 100 units and [expect to ship] 1,000 before the end of the year." Unigrid's battery is an emerging technology – it's a sodium ion, rather than lithium ion device.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sodium ion batteries have got energy storage experts excited because they could end up much cheaper to build and operate than lithium ion.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: They're potentially less likely to catch fire and should also work in a wider range of temperatures, even down to lows of minus 40C , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Darren Tan founded Unigrid - a maker of sodium ion batteries But there's a debate over what constitutes the best, and safest, sodium ion battery design.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Plus, more than one , external US company working in this space has floundered in recent years , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: China leads the world in sodium ion battery manufacturing at present so US competitors are going to have to work hard to keep up.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The prize that awaits is the possibility of batteries made in the US with 100% US-sourced materials.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: This is unlike lithium ion batteries, where China dominates the materials , external supply chain as well as manufacturing.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: For Tan, China has helped his company get to market.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The Unigrid battery currently uses sodium ion cells made there, rather than in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We can switch back and forth and choose what battery we want to work with," says Tan, explaining that, in future, his firm might source cells from the US – though these may come at a different cost.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: There's another consideration.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Unigrid's battery contains chromium-3 in its cathode.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: In a battery, electrons flow from cathode to anode , external when charging and in the opposite direction when discharging or providing power.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Ivana Hasa, at the Warwick Manufacturing Group, University of Warwick, who has no connection to Unigrid, agrees that it is possible for chromium-3 to form chromium-6 at very high states of charge, though she says this can be mitigated by how voltage is controlled within the battery.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "Safety tests reported on the cell chemistry are very promising," she says of Unigrid's tech.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Tan says concerns around toxicity of the battery's materials are "overblown" and emphasises that Unigrid's battery has passed certification and safety tests for sale in Europe and is currently undergoing such evaluations for the US market.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Third-party tests have not been able to get the battery to form chromium-6, he says.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We've tried very hard to try and produce it, we've overcharged it as much as we can...
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: We were unsuccessful in generating chromium-6." The choice of cathode material, or how the electrolyte – which separates cathode and anode – is formulated are key details influencing the performance and longevity of sodium ion batteries.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Some manufacturers are not using chromium for their cathode but hard carbon instead, or sodium iron phosphate pyrophosphate (NFPP).
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: In general, confidence around sodium ion batteries' reliability has increased during the last few years, says Prof Dame Grey, meaning they are now finding their way into grid storage applications.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Last December, LFP batteries – a relatively cheap form of lithium ion battery – were trading at $81 per kilowatt hour , external (kWh) whereas Unigrid's sodium ion battery pricing is roughly $100 kWh , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Some companies that spoke to the BBC suggested sodium ion might reach as low as $30 per kWh but analysts say significantly lower costs could be many years away , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sodium ion batteries are also not as energy dense as lithium ion batteries, meaning they must be slightly bigger and heavier in order to provide the same amount of power.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The technology has been improving , external on this front in recent years but, even so, you're not likely to see sodium ion cells in small, energy hungry devices such as smartphones.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: A Reform UK councillor filmed calling Asian homeowners "parasites" has resigned from two councils and apologised for his comments.

sentences.text: Alan Feeney, who has since stepped down from the party, was heard making the remarks during undercover filming for an ITV News investigation , external in the run up to council elections in May.
sentences.article_title: Reform councillor quits over offensive remarks

sentences.text: Feeney said he had resigned every post he held on Solihull Council and Birmingham City Council, adding that his remarks "were wrong, offensive and completely unacceptable".

sentences.article_title: Reform councillor quits over offensive remarks

sentences.article_title: Reform councillor quits over offensive remarks

sentences.text: Green leader Zack Polanski said the motion was 'imperfect' but supported the substance of it The equality watchdog has written to the Green Party asking for more information about a controversial "Zionism is racism" motion passed by members.

sentences.text: The Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC) said it recognised that "many Jewish people will be feeling vulnerable" following the motion, passed at the party's conference earlier this month.

sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

The watchdog said it would "take action where appropriate" after assessing the extra information.
sentences.article_title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens over 'Zionism is racism' motion

sentences.article_title: Burnham asks for his Widdecombe remarks to be corrected

sentences.article_title: Burnham asks for his Widdecombe remarks to be corrected

sentences.article_title: Burnham asks for his Widdecombe remarks to be corrected

sentences.text: Around 650 more prisoners in England and Wales are due to be released under the second tranche of the government's early release scheme.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Under the scheme, eligible prisoners are released after serving a third of their total custodial sentence rather than after 40% or 50% of the term.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: People sentenced for manslaughter, rape, serious child sex and grooming offences are excluded.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: This is not the first time a government - Conservative or Labour - has released prisoners early to make space in England and Wales' overcrowded prisons.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: BBC Verify has looked at the reasons why ministers say this latest scheme is necessary.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: The prison population in England and Wales on 12 October was 87,033, which was 97.8% of useable capacity , external .
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) has previously warned the prison population will overtake capacity as soon as this November.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: In the long-term the MoJ has projected that the capacity of all prisons will rise to around 99,000 by 2032 as a result of more prisons being built by this government.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: But it also projected that the prisoner population would rise to about 104,000 by 2032 if the Sentencing Act 2026 - which provides for earlier release - did not come into force.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: That is why Justice Secretary Alex Norris says there is a "prison capacity crisis" which means the government has to implement the latest early release scheme.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: In total 4,500 prisoners are due to be released early by June 2027 , external .
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: About 700 offenders were released from jail early on 1 October - all of whom were serving terms of less than 19 months.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: The MoJ has projected that the Sentencing Act will mean the prisoner population remains below the capacity of the prison system, rising only to around 96,000 by 2032.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: The England and Wales prison population has risen significantly in recent decades with a significant uptick starting in the 1990s before reaching a record high in 2024.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: The Institute for Government (IFG) think tank says this is partly the result of longer sentences.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: In 2023, the average prison sentence at Crown Courts in England and Wales - which deal with more serious offences - was more than 25% longer than those handed down in 2012.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: For some crimes, the increase was greater.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Sentences for robbery in 2023 were 13 months longer on average than in 2012 - an increase of 36%.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Longer sentences mean more people being held in prison at any one time.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Former Conservative Justice Secretary David Gauke, who led an independent sentencing review for Sir Keir Starmer's government, argues this is the result of a "bidding war" by political parties since the 1990s over who can imprison people for longer.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Gauke also points out that the prison population has been rising at a time when overall crime in England and Wales has been falling, according to the official Crime Survey.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: So despite the fall in crime more people are being sent to prison - and for longer.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Another reason for upward pressure on the prison population is that more people than before are being returned to prison for breaching the conditions of their release.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: There were 51,419 licence recalls in England and Wales in the year ending March 2026, up from 40,259 in the previous year - a 28% increase.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Cassia Rowland from the IFG said most recalls are for breaches of licence conditions, such as missed appointments, rather than offenders committing further offences or posing a serious risk to the public.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: "The probation service is overwhelmed, with high caseloads and lots of vacancies putting often inexperienced staff under huge pressure," she said.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Successive governments have pledged to increase the number of prison places - but delivery has often fallen short of those promises.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Between 2010 and 2024, when the Conservatives were in power, around 13,000 new prison places were created.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: But around 12,500 places - notably those built during the Victorian era - were closed after falling into disrepair.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: That means an estimated net total of only around 500 new prison places were added over 14 years.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: In a 2024 report, the National Audit Office (NAO) cited the MOJ's "unrealistic timelines", and government bodies not working together to prioritise delivery, as reasons for the slow pace of prison building.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Work is under way on a new prison - HMP Welland - being built in Leicestershire The MOJ say around 6,500 net prison places were created between 2022 and 2025, once closures are taken into consideration.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: These include places created in three new prisons.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: However, further expansion to existing prisons has been delayed by a major supplier going into administration, according to the Prison Reform Trust.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Pia Sinha of the Prison Reform Trust told BBC Verify: "Successive governments have found it difficult to increase prison capacity because new prisons take years to plan and build, often facing planning hurdles and local opposition." The Labour government has pledged to build 14,000 new prison places by 2031.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: Analysts argue that without a major change in thinking about the appropriateness of prison as punishment, or a significant long-term increase in prison building, the system in England and Wales will remain close to capacity.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: And that means governments will continue to be under pressure to implement early release schemes to avert a capacity crisis.
sentences.article_title: Why are hundreds of prisoners being released early?

sentences.text: NHS bosses in England say the way maternity care is organised is "not fit for purpose" with safety at risk, and warn up to 20 smaller units may have to close.

sentences.article_title: NHS bosses say smaller maternity units may have to close

sentences.article_title: NHS bosses say smaller maternity units may have to close

sentences.article_title: NHS bosses say smaller maternity units may have to close

sentences.article_title: NHS bosses say smaller maternity units may have to close

sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Willow, from Kent, was admitted to intensive care at GOSH.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Her mum, Stacey Moore, was told she had a 50% chance of survival.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: "The consultant said... we should bring our family up to say goodbye to her.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: This is how critical and in how much danger she was of passing away." The team at GOSH used metagenomics - a diagnostic test that works by sequencing all genetic material present, in contrast to conventional methods where clinicians need to decide in advance what they're looking for.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: The test identified that Willow had a drug-resistant bacterial infection which needed a different antibiotic to the one she had been prescribed.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: The test helped doctors identify which antibiotic would be effective in treating Willow "The fact that they had a test there available to her was paramount.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: It saved her life," said Stacey.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: "It's a miracle she's here and we're extremely grateful for that," added Willow's dad, Russ.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: With the right treatment, Willow was eventually able to recover from her infection, but needed several months in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: She is one of many patients at the children's hospital to benefit from the new type of testing.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: During a study in 2024-5 metagenomic testing was used on 122 critically ill children in the paediatric intensive care unit (ICU) at GOSH.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: The results have now been published in the Lancet Microbe.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Metagenomic testing analyses all genetic material in a sample and can detect thousands of different pathogens.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: By contrast, the most common method of identifying bacteria is by trying to culture them in Petri dishes, a technology that has been used since Victorian times.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Another test, PCR, can identify viruses and some bacteria, but doctors need to specify what they are trying to detect.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Metagenomics testing at GOSH was able to identify around nine in 10 bacteria and viruses and all fungi in samples.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Willow celebrated her 10th birthday in August In a quarter of cases, the results influenced prescribing decisions, including starting, stopping or changing an antibiotic.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Dr Sam Ray, consultant in paediatric intensive care medicine at GOSH and co-author of the study said traditional testing required clinicians to make an educated guess about which infection they were looking for.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: "The study has helped us to spot infections we would have missed, get children on the right treatment and stop antibiotics when we know they aren't going to work.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: "Removing unnecessary treatment is incredibly important for the fight against growing antimicrobial resistance." Metagenomic testing at GOSH also detected 50 organisms not identified by routine diagnostics, meaning it could play an early warning role against new infections.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: Dr Julianne Brown, head of the GOSH Metagenomics Service and co-senior author of the study said the new testing was being gradually rolled out to around 30 intensive care units across the UK treating both adults and children.
sentences.article_title: Ten-year-old Willow among children to benefit from pioneering same-day test to spot infections

sentences.text: "It could be a powerful tool for identifying new infections that pose a pandemic threat," she added.

sentences.text: Trans patients should be cared for on single-sex hospital wards or bays that align with their biological sex rather than their gender identity, according to new NHS England (NHSE) guidance.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: It says when this is not "clinically appropriate" then alternative arrangements should be made and the dignity and safety of all patients should be maintained.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The guidance also says staff facilities should be used by people based on their biological sex, while trusts should ensure enough alternatives to single-sex facilities, such as single-occupancy toilets, are offered.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: Previous NHSE guidance suggested patients and staff could be accommodated on wards or use facilities based on their gender identity.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: That meant that a trans woman – a biological male who identifies as a woman – could have chosen to be on a women's ward, or a trans man – a biological female who identifies as a man – could have opted for a men's ward.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: That guidance was withdrawn following the Supreme Court ruling in April 2025 that under equality law the term "sex" means biological sex and "woman" refers to a biological woman.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The judgment said for a space or service to be single sex it should only allow those of the same biological sex to use it.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: Also under the new guidance issued on Thursday, NHSE emphasised that in order to avoid discriminating against trans people they should be offered gender neutral spaces.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: But the guidance also says decisions may have to be made on a case-by-case basis and must ensure clinical needs are met.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: It also makes clear that there are circumstances where clinical need is the overriding priority, including on emergency units and urgent care settings.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: In addition to the patient document of the guidance, NHSE has published advice for trusts on how to organise changing rooms, toilets and other single-sex facilities for staff.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: Again, it says they should be used by people based on their biological sex, not their gender identity.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The document encourages NHS trusts in England to carry out an audit to ensure they are offering enough alternatives to single-sex facilities, for instance, gender neutral or single occupancy toilets.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: Pressures on hospitals mean many have already struggled to keep wards single sex.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: NHSE data shows that the number of breaches of the previous mixed-sex accommodation guidance has been growing every year since 2021- where members of the opposite sex were placed on a single-sex ward.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The most recent figure for August 2026 shows there were 5,520 breaches, compared to 3,853 in June 2025.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: Sex-based rights charity Sex Matters has welcomed the guidance as a "momentous shift back to reality", but is concerned about how it will be applied.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: "NHS patient data is a mess, with potentially thousands of trans-identifying people recorded as the opposite sex," CEO Maya Forstater said.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: Trans rights organisations TransActual and Trans+ Solidarity Alliance have said they are concerned NHS staff will be unclear on how to safely look after trans patients.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: "This guidance will not survive contact with reality in resource-strapped hospitals and will create unworkable operational challenges," they said.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The NHS has been at the centre of a number of high-profile arguments over the interpretation of equality law and workplace regulations.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: In January 2026, Darlington Memorial Hospital was found to have violated the dignity of a group of nurses who complained about a transgender colleague - a biological male who identified as a woman - being allowed to use the female changing rooms.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The nurses were told they should change somewhere else if they objected.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The tribunal concluded that the trust had indirectly discriminated against them.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The nurses are currently seeking £400,000 from the NHS to cover their legal costs.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: One of the nurses who brought the action, Bethany Hutchison, who is now president of the Darlington Nurses Union, says they welcome the "clear and necessary guidance" from NHSE, but the test will be whether trusts follow it.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: "The Darlington nurses should never have had to take their own employer to court to secure privacy, dignity and lawful single-sex facilities," she said.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: "Enforcement cannot continue to depend on the courage and personal sacrifice of individual nurses." In Scotland, another employment tribunal found, in December 2025, that a nurse, Sandie Peggie, had been harassed by NHS Fife over its interpretation of rules on single sex spaces.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: Peggie had complained about a doctor, who was a trans woman, using the female changing rooms.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: She was suspended after raising concerns.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The tribunal dismissed her other claims of discrimination and victimisation.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: An appeal is under way and expected to reach the courts next year.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: Louis, Otis and Ben all have differing opinions on whether teens should use protein powder Twelve-year-old Ben is desperate to try protein powder but there's one hurdle: me, his mum.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: "I've asked about 20 times and you just keep saying no!", he says, claiming it would make him "fitter and bigger" and that his male friends use it.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: In recent years, there's been an explosion of products marketed as "high protein", including milk, yoghurt, breads, cereals, bars and powders.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Social media is flooded with adverts for various supplements, including protein powder.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: As a health journalist, I'm sceptical and think at Ben's age he must be getting enough protein through his diet.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: So, do experts think it's safe for pre-teens and teenagers or is a big, juicy steak just as good?
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: In recent years, there has been an explosion of products marketed as "high protein"... ... however, protein is found in lots of everyday foods, including meat, fish, eggs, dairy, bread, grains and pulses My sport-obsessed son, who already eats a healthy balanced diet, asks me about protein powder on a regular basis.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: His friend Louis, 12, has been using protein powder once or twice a week for nearly a year, after a workout and on top of whole foods.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: His parents are aware of this.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: "I think it's helped, it gives me more energy and it's helped me grow, probably," he says.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: But Ben's other friend Otis, who is 13, is not keen on the idea and feels there is pressure on young people to take protein supplements.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: "They might just start using them without thinking about the consequences or what effects it may have on them." Proteins break down into amino acids that help the body grow and repair.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: But your body can't make all the amino acids it needs on its own, so you need to get more - known as essential amino acids - through your diet.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: For an adult with a healthy weight, the recommended daily amount of protein you should be eating is 0.75 grams per kg of body weight, according to the NHS.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: A good rule of thumb is that the amount of protein you have for each meal should fit into the palm of your hand.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: If you exercise a lot, and when you get older, you need more protein so you could have up to 2 grams per kg of body weight.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: But do teens really need it if they're eating well?
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: This video can not be played Do you really need protein powder to build muscle?
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: For teenage boys and girls "you can get all the protein that you need from food alone", says registered dietitian Nichola Ludlam-Raine.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: It is important that teenage girls, especially, get enough iron and calcium, so Ludlam-Raine says not to become overly focused on protein at the expense of other nutrients.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Protein shakes, powders or bars can be useful for some, including high-level athletes and those who have certain allergies, but they should not replace a healthy diet.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: There can also be some unwanted side effects from using protein powders such as bloating, gas, cramps, and diarrhoea.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Those with pre-existing health conditions should not use it unless they have been told they can by their doctor.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Ludlam-Raine points out that the protein powder market is not as tightly regulated as medicines.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: "Of course, you can get reputable companies who do third-party testing and make sure that what you see on the label is what is in the inside, but that's not always the case," she says.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: "And ultimately you can't just have a shake and your biceps grow." Some protein powders contain high amounts of added sugar, artificial ingredients, and hidden stimulants.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Dr Ramnik Mathur is a consultant paediatrician from West London.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: He explains that we need micronutrients like zinc, calcium and magnesium, which are found in whole foods.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: So, if meals are replaced with protein shakes, those nutrients are lost.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Experts suggest spreading out protein across the day and aiming for 20-25g per meal.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: If you're keen to up your intake, try some of these recipes.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: During puberty when children have growth spurts, they do need more protein because their body is growing rapidly, building new muscle and bone mass.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: But Mathur says there are risks to eating too much protein.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: "If you look at social media, they'll say you need to eat a lot of protein, but your body can handle only so much." He explains that if you eat too much, it has to be excreted by the kidneys and liver which can become overloaded and have serious health implications.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: The key takeaway from Mathur: "If a 12-year-old child is eating a healthy balanced diet then they shouldn't need any more protein." Ludlam-Raine's advice is to get teens to improve their diet first before taking any protein powder, especially regularly.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: If they still want to use it, speak to a registered dietitian or nutritionist first.
sentences.article_title: I'm 12 and I want to try protein powder - should I?

sentences.text: Now off I go to tell my son the answer is still no - and the experts say the same.

sentences.text: The amount of time children in England spend on screens at school could be harming their "physical and developmental health", a group of more than 150 clinicians has warned.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: GPs, paediatricians and other specialists said in an open letter to Education Secretary Lucy Powell and Health Secretary Yvette Cooper that tablets and laptops are being used without a full understanding of their long-term health impacts, including on eye health.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: The clinicians said they are prescribing glasses, hearing aids and speech therapy to children "for a problem that is unintentionally being made worse in our schools".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: The government said it was consulting on screen time guidance for children aged five to 18 but that technology could be a powerful learning tool if used properly.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: The group of clinicians said nearly one million children are using screens in most lessons, despite studies suggesting a rise in short-sightedness.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: They pointed to an analysis of 276 studies covering 5.4 million participants around the world.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: That analysis, they claimed, found a rise in short-sightedness among children and adolescents from around 24% in 1990 to almost 36% by 2023, warning the condition is associated with an increased risk of a range of eye health problems.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: She told BBC Radio 4's Today programme parents had not been given the chance to "opt out" of the "excessive" use of screens in schools, which risks children "just not thriving" in education.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: She said an "explosion" in short-sightedness "cannot be put down to genetics alone".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: It also warned that children with special educational needs are "disproportionately" directed to screen-based learning.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders, said education technology can provide schools with "very effective learning tools".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: But he said such technology was only part of an "overall learning strategy", which also includes classroom discussion and interaction, and that the school day also has  "plenty of non-screen time such as PE, sport, and break times with classmates".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: "We would welcome the development of practical, evidence-based guidance to support the work of schools in the use of education technology," he added.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: Paul Whiteman, general secretary of the National Association of Head Teachers, said it was "important that a healthy balance is struck", adding that "greater clarity is needed from the government on this".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: A Department for Education spokesperson said the government was developing new screen-time guidance for children aged five to 18, and will consult on the safety of artificial intelligence and educational technology in schools.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: Men's Action Network (MAN) has offered to meet James McClean after he was reported as saying he would view seeking therapy as a sign of 'weakness' A men's mental health charity has offered to meet footballer James McClean after he told a newspaper he views speaking to a psychologist as "weak".
sentences.article_title: Charity offers to meet James McClean over therapy comments

sentences.text: In an interview with the Sunday Independent , external , the Derry City player said he had never tried therapy because "as a man I would see that as a weakness".
sentences.article_title: Charity offers to meet James McClean over therapy comments

sentences.text: Michael Lynch, from Men's Action Network (MAN) based in Londonderry, said the charity would welcome the opportunity to meet with him to discuss the importance of encouraging all men to feel comfortable seeking support when they need it.
sentences.article_title: Charity offers to meet James McClean over therapy comments

sentences.text: McClean has been contacted for comment but the club has distanced itself from his views and agreed to meet MAN.
sentences.article_title: Charity offers to meet James McClean over therapy comments

sentences.text: The former Sunderland, West Bromwich Albion and Stoke City player spoke about his wife's view that he had "built-up anger and frustration" that he had blocked out, to which the interviewer asked him if he had ever tried therapy.
sentences.article_title: Charity offers to meet James McClean over therapy comments

sentences.text: McClean responded that he had heard his brother, fellow Derry City player Patrick McClean, "on a call to a club psychologist, having a lovely chat".
sentences.article_title: Charity offers to meet James McClean over therapy comments

sentences.text: "And a lot of the players speak to him and for me that's just weak.
sentences.article_title: Charity offers to meet James McClean over therapy comments

sentences.text: "As a man, I see that as weakness.
sentences.article_title: Charity offers to meet James McClean over therapy comments

sentences.text: "I see it as a weakness that I'd have to speak to someone about my feelings, my emotions." Michael Lynch says James McClean is an influential figure, particularly for young men Lynch said he would welcome a meeting with McClean to discuss his views, as first reported by Derry Now , external .
sentences.article_title: Charity offers to meet James McClean over therapy comments

sentences.text: He told BBC News NI that McClean was entitled to his views and "neither I nor anyone else is entitled to say otherwise, because men's mental health is such a complex issue".
sentences.article_title: Charity offers to meet James McClean over therapy comments

sentences.text: "In some ways, I agree with him, in the sense that he mentioned that the only person who can decide whether seeking support is right for them is the person themselves, because nobody can do it for you.
sentences.article_title: Charity offers to meet James McClean over therapy comments

sentences.text: "But what I and others involved with MAN would say is that there is certainly still a stigma around men feeling that they cannot reach out at times and say, 'I am not OK and need to seek support', when that is so far from the truth." Lynch added that "asking for help isn't a sign of weakness".
sentences.article_title: Charity offers to meet James McClean over therapy comments

sentences.text: "For men to recognise that they need support and act on it is incredibly brave." Lynch said James McClean was an influential figure, particularly for young men from Derry, given his sporting and personal achievements.
sentences.article_title: Charity offers to meet James McClean over therapy comments

sentences.text: "We would obviously welcome a meeting with someone of that stature, for him to come and meet with the people we speak with every day, and we would love for him to have a conversation with us.
sentences.article_title: Charity offers to meet James McClean over therapy comments

sentences.text: "I think it would be really beneficial for people to hear from someone who has achieved so much in his career and has been a role model for so many people, to show what can be achieved with hard work." In a statement, Derry City Football Club said McClean's views "do not reflect our core values or beliefs".
sentences.article_title: Charity offers to meet James McClean over therapy comments

sentences.text: "The club places the highest priority on the mental health and wellbeing of our players, staff and the wider Derry City community," the statement said.
sentences.article_title: Charity offers to meet James McClean over therapy comments

sentences.text: "Supported by our in-house psychologist, the club actively encourages anyone facing mental health challenges to speak openly, seek support and know they never have to face such challenges alone." James McClean has had an acclaimed club and international career, having earned 103 caps for the Republic of Ireland.

sentences.text: A million young people are being offered a free meningitis B vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It comes after concerns over the UK's largest and fastest growing outbreak that happened in Kent earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Seventeen and 18-year-olds can book via the NHS National Booking Service , external if they are already registered with a GP , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You do not need to be registered with a GP surgery to use the walk-in service.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Find a participating pharmacy here , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine, given as two doses and at least 28 days apart, is being offered to 17 and 18-year-olds in sixth form and students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Both doses are needed for the fullest protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Within weeks, in Kent, there were 29 confirmed or suspected cases and two deaths.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: That's why the new, one-off campaign is being launched - to help protect those at greatest risk and hopefully prevent something like this from happening again.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Students in their first year of university have a risk that is about seven times higher than that of young people of a similar age who do not go to university, says NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis infections can be spread through close contact - for example through kissing, sharing vapes and drinks or living in close quarters with a person with the bug.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: UK health officials say the risk to 18-year-olds or those entering university or a residential college for the first time is higher because of increased mixing of social groups and shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: MenB infection can cause serious, life-threatening problems including inflammation of the lining of the brain (meningitis) and blood poisoning (sepsis).
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can lead to life-changing disabilities such as amputations, hearing loss and brain damage, and in some cases can be fatal.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: All babies are now offered it.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But it means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide long-term protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But UK vaccine experts now say government should consider routinely offering the vaccine to all teenagers at around age 15 .

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down We know some people love a cuppa, even when it's sweltering, and that actually makes scientific sense.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Research suggests your body sweats more quickly to get rid of the excess heat after a hot drink.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So hot tea won't necessarily help you cool down more quickly - the key thing is to stay hydrated no matter the temperature of the liquid.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You don't need to shun your favourite coffee either just because it's hot - although too much caffeine can make the body produce more urine, and leave you dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: For matcha fans, the drink contains more caffeine than a cup of tea but less than a regular coffee.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Dr Daly says one or two coffees a day should make little difference to your hydration levels - but five or six will start to have an effect.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You could structure your day differently too, and take a southern European approach to eating.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Have an early breakfast, an afternoon siesta while it's very hot and then a late dinner.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave
